subject.title: refactor: move MCP OAuth state to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this immediate Doctor-only MCP OAuth cutover, where upgraded runtimes never read retired credential JSON and existing sessions remain unavailable until a verified `openclaw doctor --fix` migration succeeds?
rationale: The code can implement either boundary correctly, but only maintainers can authorize the intentional upgrade interruption and decide whether fail-closed migration of stored OAuth secrets is the desired release contract.

options.title: Accept Doctor-only cutover
options.body: Approve SQLite as the only runtime store, require release-visible Doctor guidance, and keep fail-closed migration and logout tombstones authoritative.

options.title: Require staged compatibility
options.body: Pause the PR and define a maintainer-approved transitional upgrade mode, accepting additional complexity and a competing source-of-truth risk.

options.title: Reject this boundary
options.body: Close or redesign the work if operators must never lose credential availability pending an explicit repair step.

recommendation.title: Accept Doctor-only cutover
recommendation.body: Approve SQLite as the only runtime store, require release-visible Doctor guidance, and keep fail-closed migration and logout tombstones authoritative.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor directly requested this handle’s decision on the credential migration and authorization contract.
